result.title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
result.comment: 23 pages, 4 figures, 15 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/junbolian/JointDW
result.summary: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying a chosen set of constraint families, and every candidate costs a column generation run. The choice is hard when families strengthen the bound only together, because a search that adds one family at a time then stops at the linear relaxation. The classical inequalities of lot sizing, network design and facility location rest on such zero-marginal groups. We prove that when each evaluation convexifies at most $s$ of $k$ families, any method that observes only bounds needs a covering number of evaluations, of order $k^w$, to find a hidden group of $w$ families, also on actual Dantzig-Wolfe relaxations. A prediction that misses $e$ members reduces the cost to $Θ(k^e)$, through one staged search that does not need to know $e$, so the evaluations a prediction saves measure what the predictor knows. We study two sources of predictions. A one-pass lookahead at an optimal LP dual is provably blind to groups whose families share no variable, and a language model reads the names and text of the model. JointDW verifies the prediction of the language model with the staged search and interleaves it with the lookahead at a bounded loss. Groups that strengthen the bound only jointly appear in a quarter of the MIPLIB-NL models whose bound can be improved. There the strongest language models identify them about as often as the lookahead, their predictions rest on the names for textbook models, and reasoning about doubles the accuracy of the same model. On larger models with distracting families, the lookahead finds the group in one evaluation of three families. Language models given only the text seldom name it, while one reasoning model given every coefficient names it in all but one answer and then needs fewer evaluations than the lookahead for pairs of families.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究语言模型能否指出 Dantzig-Wolfe 重整中「只有联合才强化界」的约束族分组，提出 JointDW 用分阶段搜索验证 LLM 预测并与 LP 对偶前瞻交错；同时给出仅观察界值时所需评估次数的覆盖数下界，并以预测节省的评估量衡量预测器掌握的信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 用「预测节省的搜索评估次数」量化预测所含信息、以及返回上一级联合才生效的隐藏组合，可能为核查 latent 状态的非边际信息贡献与 THINK/STOP 预算分配评价提供概念线索，但属运筹优化背景，迁移需自行判断。
